title: The <SPI.h> Library & Multi-Device Chip Selects
summary: Arbitrate multiple SPI peripherals on shared MOSI, MISO, and SCK lines using independent Chip Select pins.

steps.title: Orchestrating the Dual-Device Bus
steps.markdownContent:
### The Ultimate Bus Coexistence Challenge
Up to this point, you have tested the **MAX7219 8x8 LED Matrix** (`comp_15`) and the **RC522 RFID Reader** (`comp_23`) individually. Now comes the true test of an embedded robotics engineer: **connecting both devices to the same SPI bus at the exact same time!**

```
Arduino Uno (Master)
  Pin 11 (MOSI) ──┬─────────────────────────────► MAX7219 DIN
                  └─────────────────────────────► RC522 MOSI
  Pin 12 (MISO) ◄───────────────────────────────  RC522 MISO (MAX7219 has no MISO!)
  Pin 13 (SCK)  ──┬─────────────────────────────► MAX7219 CLK
                  └─────────────────────────────► RC522 SCK
  Pin 10 (CS1)  ────────────────────────────────► MAX7219 CS (Display Select)
  Pin 8  (CS2)  ────────────────────────────────► RC522 SDA  (RFID Select)
  Pin 9  (RST)  ────────────────────────────────► RC522 RST  (RFID Reset)
```

### The Two Golden Rules of Multi-Device SPI
1. **Shared Highways:** Pins 11 (MOSI) and 13 (SCK) branch off in parallel to both the display and the RFID reader. Pin 12 (MISO) connects directly to the RFID reader (the MAX7219 is write-only and does not use MISO).
2. **Private Door-Knockers:** Never tie CS pins together! Pin 10 independently controls the MAX7219 display, and Pin 8 independently controls the RC522 reader. By keeping one CS HIGH while the other is LOW, the Arduino switches conversations instantly without cross-talk!

quickCheck.question: When connecting both the MAX7219 LED matrix and the RC522 RFID reader to an Arduino Uno, which pins must they share in parallel?
options: They cannot share any pins; they require 8 completely independent pins
quickCheck.explanation: MOSI (Pin 11) and SCK (Pin 13) form the shared high-speed data and clock highways used by both peripherals.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Remember: in an SPI bus, clock (SCK) and outward data (MOSI) are shared across all connected devices.

quickCheck.question: Why is the MAX7219 display able to share the bus without connecting to Pin 12 (MISO)?
options: The MAX7219 is a write-only display that receives pixel data but never transmits bytes back to the Arduino
Because MISO only works with motors
quickCheck.explanation: Display drivers like the MAX7219 are write-only devices, leaving the MISO return line completely free for input sensors like the RC522.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: You look at a display, but a display doesn't need to report readings back to you: data flows one way from Uno to screen.

steps.title: Breadboard Bus Distribution Schematic
steps.markdownContent:
### Dual-Voltage Power Distribution Architecture
Notice the crucial power difference between our two components:
- **MAX7219 LED Matrix:** Requires **+5V** to drive 64 bright LEDs.
- **RC522 RFID Reader:** Requires **+3.3V ONLY**!

```
POWER DISTRIBUTION:
  Uno 5V   ──► Breadboard Red Rail (+) ──► MAX7219 VCC (5V)
  Uno 3.3V ──────────────────────────────► RC522 VCC (3.3V DIRECT!)
  Uno GND  ──► Breadboard Blue Rail (-)─┬► MAX7219 GND
                                        └► RC522 GND

SPI SIGNAL DISTRIBUTION:
  Uno Pin 11 (MOSI) ──► Breadboard Row 25 ─┬► MAX7219 DIN
                                           └► RC522 MOSI
  Uno Pin 13 (SCK)  ──► Breadboard Row 26 ─┬► MAX7219 CLK
                                           └► RC522 SCK
  Uno Pin 12 (MISO) ───────────────────────► RC522 MISO
  Uno Pin 10 (CS1)  ───────────────────────► MAX7219 CS
  Uno Pin 8  (CS2)  ───────────────────────► RC522 SDA (CS)
  Uno Pin 9  (RST)  ───────────────────────► RC522 RST
```

### Interactive Arbitrator Lab
Test bus arbitration in the simulator below. Toggle between CS1 and CS2 to verify that activating one peripheral automatically holds the other in tri-state standby!

interactiveConfig.question: How do you ensure the RC522 RFID reader does not interfere with transmissions to the MAX7219 LED matrix?
options: Hold the RC522's Chip Select pin HIGH while pulling the MAX7219's Chip Select pin LOW
Unplug the RFID module's ground wire before updating the screen
Set the microcontroller clock frequency to zero
interactiveConfig.explanation: Holding the RC522 CS pin HIGH places its MISO output into high-impedance (Hi-Z) standby, preventing any interference.

questions.question: How do you ensure the RC522 RFID reader does not interfere with transmissions to the MAX7219 LED matrix?
options: Hold the RC522's Chip Select pin HIGH while pulling the MAX7219's Chip Select pin LOW
Unplug the RFID module's ground wire before updating the screen
Set the microcontroller clock frequency to zero
questions.explanation: Holding the RC522 CS pin HIGH places its MISO output into high-impedance (Hi-Z) standby, preventing any interference.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to connect the RC522 VCC pin to the breadboard +5V power rail?
options: The RC522 is strictly a 3.3V component; 5V will permanently burn out its silicon radio circuitry
5V will cause the breadboard wires to turn blue
The LEDs on the MAX7219 will dim slightly
questions.explanation: The MFRC522 IC is rated for 3.3V maximum supply voltage. Over-voltage damages the sensitive RF transceiver circuits.

questions.question: Why must an Arduino engineer configure all CS pins to OUTPUT and HIGH during the early lines of setup()?
options: To keep all connected peripherals in high-impedance standby until the microcontroller is ready to speak to them
To clear out remaining electrical charge from previous days
Because inputs cannot be connected to digital pins
questions.explanation: Setting CS pins HIGH immediately puts all peripherals into dormant standby, avoiding spurious bus contention during bootup.
